title: Altars ‘of’ Saints: same stone is God’s altar and a martyr’s tomb—dedication to Saints only under tomb-ratio, else idolatry
source_text: XXI. Quod spectat ad altaria, quae de Sanctorum quoque nomine appellantur, & dicuntur illis esse consecrata, Notat similiter Bellarminus unum eundemque lapidem dici altare, quatenus in eo sacrificatur Deo; & eundem dici tumulum vel sepulchrum, quatenus tegit ossa Martyris alicujus. Omnia enim altaria esse sepulchra Sanctorum. Jam vero quae dicuntur altaria dicari Sanctis, non sub ratione altaris, sed sub ratione sepulchri. Nam esse Idololatriam erigere Sanctis altaria; sed tamen non esse Idololatriam, erigere illis lapideos tumulos.
pass_a_gloss: As regards altars, which are also called by the Saints’ names and said to be consecrated to them, Bellarmine likewise notes that one and the same stone is called an altar insofar as God is sacrificed upon it; and the same is called a tumulus or sepulcher insofar as it covers the bones of some Martyr. For all altars are sepulchers of the Saints. Now indeed those which are said to be dedicated to the Saints as altars are dedicated not under the reason of an altar, but under the reason of a sepulcher. For it is Idolatry to erect altars to the Saints; but yet it is not Idolatry to erect stone tumuli to them.
pass_b_english: One stone: altar to God, tomb over a martyr’s bones—every altar a Saint’s sepulcher.
Dedication ‘to Saints’ is licit only as tomb-ratio; altar-ratio to Saints would be idolatry.

lemmas.gloss: under the reason of an altar
under the reason of a sepulcher
